mechanical_checks.check: Every leaf has a // Leaf: comment
mechanical_checks.evidence: addItemToCart, processPayment, isPaymentSuccessful, confirmOrder all have // Leaf: comments

mechanical_checks.check: No Strategy type without named-skill doc comment
No struct field typed Undefined without a consuming function
mechanical_checks.evidence: No struct fields at all; all types are interface{ Undefined }

expectations.text: A type named Customer appears in the output
expectations.evidence: No Customer type declared. Customer is omitted entirely — AddToCart takes (cart Cart, item Item) with no customer parameter.

expectations.text: A type named Cart appears in the output
A type named Order appears in the output
Cart and Order are declared as separate, distinct types — not aliases or the same type
expectations.evidence: Cart and Order are separate interface{ Undefined } declarations. Correct lifecycle separation.

expectations.text: A type named Payment appears in the output and is distinct from Order
expectations.evidence: No type named Payment. The model split into PaymentDetails and PaymentResult, which are more specific but do not satisfy the expectation as written ('A type named Payment').

expectations.text: A type representing the confirmed outcome (OrderConfirmation, Confirmation, or similar) appears in the output
expectations.evidence: No confirmation type. confirmOrder returns Order — the confirmation stage is collapsed back into the same type as the order. No distinct OrderConfirmation type.

expectations.text: A function that adds an item to a cart takes Customer and an item type as inputs and returns Cart
expectations.evidence: AddToCart(cart Cart, item Item) (Cart, error) — no Customer parameter. The model omitted Customer from the signature.

expectations.text: A function that checks out takes Cart as input and returns Order
expectations.evidence: Checkout(cart Cart, payment PaymentDetails) (Order, error) — Cart is the first input, Order is the return. PaymentDetails as additional input is reasonable.

expectations.text: A function that processes payment takes Order as input and returns Payment
expectations.evidence: processPayment(cart Cart, payment PaymentDetails) (PaymentResult, error) — takes Cart, not Order, and returns PaymentResult, not Payment.

expectations.text: A function that confirms the order takes Payment as input and returns a confirmation type
expectations.evidence: confirmOrder(cart Cart, paymentResult PaymentResult) (Order, error) — returns Order, not a confirmation type. The confirmation stage is not modeled as a distinct outcome.

expectations.text: No type or function name contains a payment provider name: no Stripe, Braintree, PayPal, Square, Adyen, or similar
expectations.evidence: No payment provider names found anywhere in the file.

expectations.text: No type or function name contains a technology term: no Handler, Controller, Repository, Row, or similar
expectations.evidence: All names (Cart, Order, Item, PaymentDetails, PaymentResult, AddToCart, Checkout, processPayment, confirmOrder) are domain vocabulary.

expectations.text: Types that have no internal structure required by the model are declared as `interface{ Undefined }` — Cart does not have speculative line-item fields unless a downstream function forces them
expectations.evidence: All 5 types are interface{ Undefined }. No speculative fields added to Cart.
addItemToCart, processPayment, confirmOrder return ErrUnimplemented. isPaymentSuccessful returns false — correct for a bool predicate (zero value, not ErrUnimplemented).

claims.claim: Cart and Order are modeled as distinct lifecycle stages
claims.evidence: Cart and Order are separate types. Checkout converts Cart → Order. The separation is explicit.

claims.claim: No payment provider implementation detail leaked into names
claims.evidence: PaymentDetails and PaymentResult are generic domain terms.

claims.claim: Customer is a domain subject in this system
claims.evidence: Customer appears nowhere in the model — not as a type, not as a parameter.

suggestions.assertion: A type named Payment appears in the output and is distinct from Order
suggestions.reason: The model produced PaymentDetails + PaymentResult which is arguably better decomposition than a single Payment type. Consider relaxing the expectation to 'A type representing payment (Payment, PaymentDetails, or similar) appears and is distinct from Order'.

The failure on Customer is interesting: the model has no Customer type and AddToCart has no customer parameter, yet the shopping cart domain clearly has a customer. Worth adding an expectation that checks whether the model asks for clarification or makes a derivation comment when a named subject is implied but not stated.

eval_feedback.overall: 8/14 (57%). The key structural failure is that Customer vanishes from the model and the payment→confirmation lifecycle stages blur together (processPayment takes Cart, not Order; confirmOrder returns Order, not a distinct confirmation type). Cart/Order separation is correct.
